newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak blue chips mixed, SAX index dips 0.14 pts.
newsitem.headline: Slovak blue chips mixed, SAX index dips 0.14 pts.

text.p: Slovak blue chips closed mixed in thinner trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Thursday, with the SAX index easing 0.14 points to 204.51.
Steel producer VSZ closed down 22 crowns at 648, which brokers said was the main factor influencing the direction of the index.

"VSZ's decline was unexpected and we do not see any rational reasons for (it)," said Jozef Cimra of ING Barings, adding that from the long-term perspective, VSZ was still considered a good share with growth potential.

Oil refiner Slovnaft closed unchanged at 910 crowns, with brokers saying the current dearth of interest in the issue may have been caused by the company's recently published lower profit figures for the first half of 1996.
Oil and gas storage company Nafta gained 10 to close at 1,910 crowns, and brokers remained bullish over the issue, though it has not traded large volumes in the past few days.

"Though the new majority owners of Nafta bought it at a discount rate, or maybe just because of it, there should be no need for them to channel out the company's profits, and the share is still a good issue," Cimra said.

Earlier this year a little known firm, Druha Obchodna a.s., bought a 45.9 percent stake from the National Property Fund in Nafta for 500 million crowns, while the market value of the stake was some 3.2 billion crowns.
Slovakia's largest commercial bank VUB gained 20 crowns to close at 1,770.
Overall volume decreased to 315,326 shares, from 549,859 shares traded on Wednesday. Turnover fell to 96.31 million crowns, from 325.55 million.
